turns.merchant: My watering can keeps getting flagged for availability. What's going on?

Your 1 product is disapproved because the availability in your product data does not match your website ([Availability in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12470049)). Here is the affected product:

- Galvanised Watering Can, 2 Gallon (HG-511): Feed says in_stock but the product page says out_of_stock.

Your automatic availability updates are already on. According to the help docs, automatic updates are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products, and they can fail if your product pages have missing, incomplete, or incorrect structured data (schema.org markup), or if the number of mismatches becomes too large ([Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284)). 

To fix this manually, change the availability in your product data to match what is on the product page, then upload the corrected data ([Availability in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12470049)). After you update your products, Google checks them again, which usually finishes within 24 to 48 hours ([What happens after you fix a product](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12153802)). Would you like to move on to the next issue?

For the price mismatches, your feed prices do not match your website prices for the following products: Beeswax Pillar Candle, 3 x 6 inch (HG-501) where the feed price is 24.00 USD but your page shows 28.00 USD, and Soy Tea Lights, Pack of 12 (HG-502) where the feed price is 12.00 USD but your page shows 14.50 USD. According to [Price in the feed does not match the website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12159029), the price you send must match the price on the product page and at checkout. To fix this, change the price in your product data so it matches the product page exactly, then upload the corrected data. Since your automatic price updates are currently turned off, you can also turn on automatic item updates as described in [Automatic item updates for price and availability](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/3246284) to help avoid these mismatches, though it is not a replacement for keeping your data up to date. After you update your products, Google checks them again, usually within 24 to 48 hours, as explained in [What happens after you fix a product](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/12153802). Would you like to move on to the missing shipping issue?

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Merchant Center can update some product information automatically, using what it finds on your website. Automatic item updates cover price, sale price, availability and condition.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: It works by reading the structured data (schema.org markup) on your product pages, and other information on the page. If your product data says one thing and the website says another, for example $4 in your data but $3 on the page, the product is updated to match the website. This helps avoid some price and availability mismatches.

results.title: Automatic item updates for price and availability
results.passage: Automatic updates are not a replacement for keeping your product data up to date. They are meant for occasional mismatches on a small share of products. If a price or availability changes often, for example more than once a day, the product may be disapproved instead of updated.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: The price you send must match the price shown on the product's page and at checkout, in the same currency. If they differ, Google disapproves the product.

results.title: Price in the feed does not match the website
results.passage: Common causes are a delay between changing the price on your website and updating your product data, a sale price with the wrong dates, or price markup on the page that differs from the price shoppers see.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Every product needs a title, and it can be at most 150 characters long.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: A good title says clearly what the product is, using specific words. Include the brand and key details such as size, color and material, especially when they tell variants apart.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: Do not put prices, shipping details or promotional text in the title. Avoid all capital letters, symbols, HTML and extra spaces.

results.title: Product title
results.passage: To fix a title that is too long, shorten it to 150 characters or less and keep the most important details near the start.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: A GTIN is the barcode number a manufacturer gives a product, such as a UPC in North America or an EAN in Europe. Google recommends sending it for every product that has one.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Products with a missing or wrong GTIN may get limited visibility. If a product does have a GTIN and you leave it out, the product could be disapproved.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Valid GTINs are 8, 12, 13 or 14 digits long. Spaces and dashes are ignored. The last digit is a check digit and must be correct, so copy the number exactly from the packaging or from your supplier.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: Only send a GTIN you are sure is right, and never make one up. Numbers starting with 02, 04 or 2 are restricted, and numbers starting with 05, 98 or 99 are coupon numbers, so neither kind is accepted.

results.title: Product barcode number (GTIN)
results.passage: If a product really has no GTIN, such as a store brand or private label item, do not send one. Send the brand and the manufacturer part number (MPN) instead.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: The identifier exists setting tells Google that a product has no unique product identifiers at all: no GTIN, no MPN and no brand.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Set it to "no" only for products that truly have none, such as custom made goods, handmade or one of a kind items, and vintage or antique items.

results.title: Products that have no barcode (identifier exists)
results.passage: Only use "no" when you are certain. If Google finds evidence that the product does have identifiers, the product gets a warning.

results.title: Misrepresentation and account suspension
results.passage: Google's misrepresentation policy does not allow listings that leave out important information or mislead shoppers about the product or the business. For example, payment terms, shipping costs and what happens after purchase must be shown clearly before the shopper commits to buy.

results.title: Misrepresentation and account suspension
results.passage: Most violations start with a warning email that gives the merchant time to fix the problem. Serious violations can lead to the account being suspended straight away, without a warning.

results.title: Misrepresentation and account suspension
results.passage: To fix the problem, update your website and your product data so they follow the policy. After that, you can ask Google to review the account.
